meta.title: Cerumen removal & cutaneous I&D — clean-room decision tables
meta.derivedFrom: cerumen-id-cleanroom-spec.md (rule numbers cited per row as specRef)

semantics.rowLookup: Rows are evaluated top-down; 'when' is a conjunction of exact-equality tests on declared facts; a fact omitted from 'when' is a wildcard; the FIRST matching row wins; 'output' is opaque data returned to the caller. No expressions, no computation.
semantics.threshold: One integer fact banded into contiguous ranges by 'bands' (min/max inclusive, null = unbounded); the matching band's 'output' is returned.
semantics.unitCaps: Per-code maximum billable units per date of service; caps are absolute inputs to claim assembly, never computed.
semantics.docChecklist: All listed items are required documentation for the code; items are human-verified, not computed.
semantics.payerNotes: Free-text constraints surfaced to the human coder; never evaluated.
semantics.chaining: A matched row/band output whose flags contain 'proceed:<tableId>' transfers evaluation to that table (rowLookup or threshold alike); bare 'proceed' means the next code-emitting rowLookup in document order. An output with no proceed flag settles evaluation: its codes (possibly empty) are the emission.

outputConventions.codes: array of {code, units, modifiers[]} claim lines; empty array = no procedure code (E/M pathway per notes)
outputConventions.flags: blocking or advisory strings the caller must surface; 'blocked:*' means do not emit procedure codes

facts.name: impaction_basis
facts.description: Which CPT Assistant impaction consideration is documented (visual = cerumen impairs exam of canal/TM/middle ear; qualitative = hard/dry/irritative causing symptoms; inflammatory = foul odor/infection/dermatitis; quantitative = obstructive copious cerumen needing magnification+instrumentation). 'none' = cerumen not impacted. Spec A1.1.

facts.name: left_ear_method
facts.description: Removal method actually used on the LEFT ear ('both' = irrigation and instrumentation on this ear). Spec A2.

facts.name: right_ear_method
facts.description: Removal method actually used on the RIGHT ear. Spec A2.

facts.name: instrumentation_by_qhp
facts.description: Any instrument-based removal was personally performed by the physician/QHP (not delegated to staff). Required for 69210. Spec A2.5.

facts.name: payer_type
facts.description: Medicare Part B vs all other payers. Drives bilateral reporting. Spec A3.

facts.name: em_separately_identifiable
facts.description: A significant, separately identifiable E/M unrelated to the decision to remove cerumen was performed and documented (clinician attestation; AAO-HNS 4-part test). Spec A4.

output.note: Non-impacted cerumen removal is part of the E/M service; no procedure code.
Instrument removal not personally performed by physician/QHP cannot be billed as 69210; if irrigation alone removed the impaction re-enter with method=irrigation, else E/M only.
Passes gate; consult cerumen.claimLines.

tables.note: Apply only after cerumen.gate returns 'proceed'. 'both' method on an ear codes as instrumentation (irrigation is included in 69210 for that ear, spec A2.3). Same-ear 69209+69210 can never be emitted because each ear yields exactly one code (CPT parenthetical enforced structurally; NO NCCI PTP edit exists to catch it downstream, spec B3.1).

output.note: Bilateral irrigation: single line, modifier 50, 1 unit (Medicare pays 150%, bilat indicator 1; commercial payers may prefer LT/RT lines — see payerNotes).
Medicare special rule: bilateral 69210 = one line, one unit, NO modifier 50 (bilat indicator 2; -50 claims are denied entirely).
CPT default; some commercial payers want LT/RT lines instead — see payerNotes.
Different methods on different ears: both codes, laterality modifiers; some payers want 59/XS on the second line.

tables.note: Required ICD-10 linkage; laterality-specific codes only (H61.20 unspecified is NOT on the MAC covered list). Spec A5.

output.note: Right ear treated → impacted cerumen, right ear.
Left ear treated → impacted cerumen, left ear.
Both ears treated → impacted cerumen, bilateral.
E/M reportable with modifier 25; documentation must satisfy the checklist and (for Medicare) the AAO-HNS 4-part test.
Sole-reason cerumen visit: procedure code only, no E/M.

required: Ear(s) treated identified (left/right/both)
Impaction finding documented (which consideration: visual/qualitative/inflammatory/quantitative)
Method documented: irrigation/lavage, solution, cerumenolytic agent if used
Performer and supervision documented (staff-performed permissible under physician/QHP supervision)
Post-procedure otoscopic check confirming removal / canal status
ICD-10 H61.21/H61.22/H61.23 matching treated ear(s)
Note signed and dated
Ear(s) treated identified (left/right/both)
Impaction finding documented (which consideration)
Instruments named (curette/spoon/hook/forceps/suction) and visualization/magnification documented (otoscope/microscope)
Removal personally performed by physician/QHP and attributed to them in the note
Time/effort indicating clinician skill was required
Post-removal exam of canal and tympanic membrane, status noted
ICD-10 H61.21/H61.22/H61.23 matching treated ear(s)
Note signed and dated
If E/M also billed: separately identifiable E/M documentation supporting modifier 25

notes: Medicare bilateral 69210: one line, one unit, no modifier 50 — MACs deny -50 claims entirely (bilat surgery indicator 2). Spec A3.3.
Medicare bilateral 69209: one line, modifier 50, one unit; paid at 150% (bilat surgery indicator 1). Spec A3.2.
Commercial payers vary on bilateral format: single line -50 vs two lines LT/RT — check the payer contract. Spec A3.1.
No NCCI PTP edit exists between 69209 and 69210 (or between either code and E/M): the same-ear prohibition and E/M bundling must be enforced by this engine, not by claim edits. Spec B3.
Audiologists may not bill 69209/69210 under Medicare; cerumen removal is included in their diagnostic testing. Spec A2.6.
G0268 (Medicare): physician removal of impacted cerumen on the same date as employed audiologist's audiologic function testing; one unit covers one or both ears. Spec A6.
Both codes have global period 000 (minor procedure): decision-to-perform E/M is bundled; modifier 25 requires a significant, separately identifiable E/M. Spec A4.1.
H61.20 (impacted cerumen, unspecified ear) is not on the MAC covered-dx list — always code laterality. Spec A5.1 / open question 4.

facts.name: lesion_type
facts.description: abscess_cyst_purulent covers the 10060 descriptor list: carbuncle, suppurative hidradenitis, cutaneous/subcutaneous abscess, cyst, furuncle, paronychia. Spec A7.

facts.name: approach
facts.description: puncture_aspiration = needle only, no incision made. Spec A7.3.

facts.name: lesion_count
facts.description: Number of distinct lesions treated at this session. Spec A8.2.

facts.name: packing_placed
facts.description: Packing placed for continuous drainage. Complicating feature. Spec A8.1.

facts.name: drain_placed
facts.description: Drain/drainage tube (e.g., Penrose) placed. Complicating feature. Spec A8.1.

facts.name: multiple_incisions
facts.description: More than one incision required to achieve full drainage of a lesion. Complicating feature. Spec A8.1.

facts.name: loculations_probed
facts.description: Probing performed to break up loculations. Complicating feature. Spec A8.1.

facts.name: tissue_excision_or_closure
facts.description: Tissue excision, primary closure, or Z-plasty required (or later surgical closure planned). Complicating feature. Spec A8.1.

facts.name: same_site_other_procedure
facts.description: Another procedure (excision/repair/destruction/removal) was performed at the same anatomic site this encounter, or the I&D was done to gain access for another procedure. Spec A7.6/A7.7.

facts.name: em_separately_identifiable
facts.description: A significant, separately identifiable E/M beyond the decision to perform the I&D was performed and documented. Spec A9.2.

output.note: I&D at the same site/encounter as another procedure, or done for access, is not separately reportable (NCCI Ch3 D).
Aspiration of a post-op wound infection has no clean fit in this family.
One unit per distinct lesion aspirated, up to the unit cap; do not also report an I&D code for the same lesion.
Hematoma aspiration codes 10160 (descriptor includes hematoma).
Applies regardless of packing or closure method; no 'complicated' tier exists for 10140.
Bulla is in the 10160 descriptor but not the 10060 descriptor list; incision of a bulla has no verified mapping.

tables.note: Reached from id.gate's incised-purulent-lesion row; band 'single' chains to id.abscessComplexity, band 'multiple' emits 10061 directly.

output.note: Multiple abscesses at one session -> 10061, never 10060 x units.

tables.note: Applies to band=single from id.abscessLesionCountBand; band=multiple emits 10061 directly from that band's output and never reaches this table. Any one complicating feature -> complicated. CPT/CMS give no official definition of 'complicated' (spec open question 1) — these five features are the secondary-source consensus.

output.note: Single lesion, single incision, no complicating features -> simple.

tables.note: Reached from id.gate's puncture-aspiration rows: 10160 units = distinct lesions aspirated, capped at the MUE (3). The cap value is duplicated from id.unitCaps because the vocabulary cannot compute min(count, cap).

output.note: More than 3 distinct lesions aspirated: MUE (MAI 3) caps billable units at 3; the excess denies but is appealable with records.

tables.note: Reached from id.gate's hematoma/seroma/fluid incision row: 10140 units = distinct collections evacuated, capped at the MUE (2). Cap value duplicated from id.unitCaps (no computation in the vocabulary).

output.specRef: B8 (up to 2 distinct collections/day, each documented)

output.note: More than 2 distinct collections: MUE (MAI 3) caps billable units at 2; the excess denies but is appealable with records.
Active NCCI PTP edits bundle 99211-99215 into every family code (mod 1) — modifier 25 required; new-patient 99202-99205 have no PTP edit but the same global-surgery policy applies.
Decision-to-perform E/M is included in the minor procedure.

required: Site/location of each lesion (anatomic specificity)
Lesion type (abscess/cyst/furuncle vs hematoma/seroma/fluid vs bulla)
Size and characteristics; single vs multiple; depth (superficial vs deep subcutaneous)

Pre-operative size, location and appearance of the lesion; approximate quantity (e.g., 1 cc, 5 mL) and quality (e.g., serous, sero-sanguinous, frank pus, malodorous) of the material drained (NGS A56766 documentation requirement). Spec B6.
Technique: incision(s) (number, size) or needle puncture; drainage achieved; irrigation/curettage/probing described
Anesthesia used (bundled but documented)
Culture obtained yes/no (specimen collection is bundled)
Wound disposition: left open / packed (material, amount) / drain placed / closed
Post-procedure assessment (hemostasis, wound appearance) and aftercare instructions

The complicating element stated concretely: packing placed (what/how much), drain placed, 'multiple incisions required to achieve full drainage', loculations probed/broken, tissue excision/closure — or >=2 distinct lesions drained

Medical necessity for draining the hematoma/seroma/fluid collection stated (e.g., severe pain, infection, failure to resolve with conservative measures) — most do not require drainage and drainage can increase infection risk (NGS A56766). Spec B6.
Needle/puncture approach documented with NO incision
What was aspirated and the volume
If units > 1: each distinct lesion aspirated documented separately
Postoperative wound infection of a prior surgical wound identified
Complex work described: suture/staple removal and/or re-incision, drainage, necrotic tissue excision, packing/drain placement
Not performed at the same encounter as the surgery that caused the infection

notes: All five codes carry a 10-day global period: routine wound checks, packing removal/repacking, and related E/M within 10 days are included (99024 for tracking only). Spec A9.
PTP: 10061 x 10060 is modifier-indicator 1 ('more extensive procedure') — payable together only for documented distinct lesions with 59/XS; same-session multiples belong in 10061 alone. Spec B7.1.

PTP: 10160 x 10061 and 10160 x 10140 are modifier-indicator 1 (mutually exclusive) — aspiration + incision codes require distinct lesions + NCCI modifier. No PTP edit exists for 10160 x 10060; the same-lesion prohibition there must be enforced by this engine. Spec B7.2.
PTP: every family code x 99211-99215 is an active modifier-1 edit — same-day established-patient E/M requires modifier 25 and separately identifiable documentation. Spec B7.3.
PTP: 10060/10061 x 97597/97598 (mod 1) — active-wound-care debridement is bundled into same-lesion I&D; 11042 x 10060 (mod 1) bundles I&D into same-site debridement. Spec B7.4.
PTP: 10140 x 76942 (ultrasound guidance) is a modifier-1 edit; no such edit exists for 10060/10061/10160 — imaging guidance billing is payer-dependent. Spec B7.5.

Local anesthesia, skin prep, irrigation, cultures, drain/packing insertion AND removal, and dressings are integral to the procedure (NCCI Ch1 integral-services list) — never separately coded. Spec A8.4.
Bilateral surgery indicator is 0 for all five codes — modifier 50 does not apply; distinct lesions use units (within MUE) or 59/XS lines. Spec B9.
MAI-2 caps (10060/10061) are absolute per-day policy edits; MAI-3 caps (10140/10160/10180) deny above the cap but are appealable with records. Spec B8.

NGS A56766 utilization guidance: repeat I&D of the same anatomic location needs a documented reason for recurrence and prevention measures; >2 drainages of the same location per year is presumed not medically necessary (hidradenitis L73.2 excepted). Spec B6.
'Complicated' has no CPT/CMS definition — payer adjudication of edge cases varies; document the complicating feature explicitly. Spec open question 1.
